checkers.name: Checkers
checkers.blurb: Jump and crown against the computer.

reversi.name: Reversi

gomoku.name: Gomoku
gomoku.blurb: Five in a row on a 15 × 15 board.

checkers.a1: Each side has 12 pieces on the dark squares. Black moves first. Pieces move one square diagonally forward and capture by jumping over an opponent's piece to the empty square beyond it. Take all the other side's pieces, or leave them with no move, to win.
checkers.a2: Yes. If a capture is possible you must take it, and a jump that can continue must go on to the end. When there are several captures you may choose any of them.
checkers.q3: How does a piece become a king?
checkers.a3: A piece that reaches the far row is crowned and its move ends there. A king moves and captures diagonally forwards and backwards, one square at a time.
checkers.q4: When is the game a draw?
checkers.a4: When 40 moves by each side pass with no capture and no new king.
checkers.a5: American checkers, also called English draughts: an 8 × 8 board, kings that move one square, and forced captures.

reversi.a1: Place a disc so that it traps a straight line of the other side's discs between it and one of yours, across, down or diagonally. All trapped discs flip to your colour. Black moves first.
reversi.a2: If you have no move that flips a disc, your turn passes to the other side. The page does this for you and says so.
reversi.a3: When neither side can move, usually because the board is full. The side with more discs wins.
reversi.a4: Corners can never be flipped, so they are the most valuable squares. Avoid the squares next to an empty corner, and try to keep your opponent's choices few.
reversi.a5: Easy plays almost at random, medium weighs good squares, and hard looks several moves ahead and plays the last moves perfectly.

gomoku.a1: Black and White take turns placing a stone on an empty point of the 15 × 15 board. The first to get five stones in an unbroken line, across, down or diagonally, wins.
gomoku.q2: Do six in a row count?
gomoku.a2: Yes. This page plays the free-style rule, so five or more stones in a row win.
gomoku.a3: Black always moves first. Choose White to let the computer start.
gomoku.a4: Watch for open threes and fours, lines with both ends free, and block them at once. Making two threats with one stone usually wins.
gomoku.q5: Is this the same as five in a row or caro?
gomoku.a5: Yes. Gomoku is also known as five in a row, and in Vietnam a similar game is called caro.

checkers.s1b: Play the computer at easy, medium or hard as Black or White, or two players on one screen.
checkers.s2b: Tap a piece, then a marked square. Captures are required; a multi-jump goes hop by hop.
checkers.s3b: Reach the far row to make a king. Take every piece or block every move to win.

reversi.s1b: Play the computer at easy, medium or hard, or two players on one screen.
reversi.s2b: Tap a marked square to place a disc and flip every line you trap.
reversi.s3b: When neither side can move, the side with more discs wins.

gomoku.s1b: Play the computer at easy, medium or hard, or two players on one screen.
gomoku.s2b: Tap an empty point to place a stone. Black moves first.
gomoku.s3b: Five or more stones in a line wins. Block your opponent's open threes and fours.
